subject.title: fix(cron): default deleteAfterRun for isolated cron jobs

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs default to cleanup across fresh and existing persisted jobs, or should recurring `deleteAfterRun` be rejected as a one-shot-only lifecycle flag?
rationale: Both choices are plausible and represented by open PRs; automation cannot safely decide whether to preserve recurring cleanup semantics or enforce a stricter public cron API contract.

options.title: Complete recurring cleanup
options.body: Keep this PR's direction, add persisted-load or doctor/upgrade handling for omitted legacy jobs, and reconcile the strict-validation PR against that decision.

options.title: Choose one-shot-only validation
options.body: Pause or close this PR and continue through the strict-validation path after its caller, Gateway error mapping, and upgrade-recovery blockers are fixed.

options.title: Accept fresh-create-only behavior
options.body: Allow this PR to change only new jobs, but explicitly document that existing omitted recurring isolated jobs require operator action or a separate migration.

recommendation.title: Complete recurring cleanup
recommendation.body: Keep this PR's direction, add persisted-load or doctor/upgrade handling for omitted legacy jobs, and reconcile the strict-validation PR against that decision.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant history points to recurring work across cron normalization, store encoding, and user-facing cron defaults, making this the best available routing owner for the contract choice.
